root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward strength and safeguarding: giving force, reinforcing, or protecting something.
root_idea.development: The semantic field develops from inherent strength to strengthening and aiding persons, and to protective supports, barriers, refuges, and fortifications.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form أَيَّدَ.
Displayed under the normalized nominal citation form أَيْدٌ, represented in the Quran in inflected forms.

senses.definition: To strengthen or empower someone by imparting force.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively for giving substantial strength or power; the Quranic construction أَيَّدْتُكَ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ expresses strengthening through the Holy Spirit.

senses.definition: To support or aid someone, especially to help accomplish an undertaking or to grant victory.
senses.usage_conditions: The supported person may be aided in an affair or helped to prevail; the construction أَيَّدَهُ عَلَى الأَمْرِ expresses aid toward accomplishing an affair, while support associated with divine victory is also attested.
Used in constructions describing possession of strength and acting with strength, including ذُو الْأَيْدِ and بِأَيْدٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become strong; to become possessed of strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I verb, also used of a thing that becomes strong.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong or mighty; an epithet for one characterized by strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to God or to a human being; the poetic example presents a strong agent as one who strings a bow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is frequently present at the morning and evening meals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression describing repeated attendance at meals.
An intransitive Form V usage, applied to a person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A means of strengthening, guarding, defending, protecting, veiling, or concealing; hence shelter, shade, or refuge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Names something that protects or reinforces a person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A supporting side or flank; an adjacent area; or a wing of an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The spatial senses include either side of something, its vicinity, and the wing or flank of an army.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reinforcing embankment or defensive structure, including an earthwork around a watering place or tent, a fortification, or a fortified and difficult-to-access mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The structure strengthens or protects what it surrounds or occupies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An elevated tract or heap of sand.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explained by the notion that camels strengthen their owner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great, mighty, or severe thing; a calamity; or anything rendered strong, hard, or severe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal or adjectival usage describing either the severity of a thing or a state made hard or severe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strengthened or aided; hence victorious; also structurally strong when applied to a building.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-result adjective or participle, with the building sense referring to physical soundness.
An active participial usage describing one who or something that strengthens or aids.

cautions: A reported variant reading of 5:110 is not treated as a separate public form because the canonical QAC form is أَيَّدَ.
The expression وَلا يَؤُدُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا is discussed as belonging to the separate root أود, meaning to burden or weigh down, and is not assigned to أيد.
